name: Revisionism (Marxism)
summary: Revisionism is Eduard Bernstein's revision of Marxism in the German Social Democratic Party around 1896-1914. It rejects the expected collapse of capitalism, growing immiseration and the dictatorship of the proletariat, and holds that socialism is reached step by step through democracy, universal suffrage, trade unions, consumer co-operatives and municipal reform, with democracy as both its means and its substance. Bernstein called socialists the heirs of liberalism, put ethics beside economic necessity, accepted national defence and a reformed colonial policy, and later condemned Bolshevik dictatorship.
scope: Bernstein's revisionism as its defining sources describe it: Steger's encyclopedia entry, Engehausen's account of the 'Revisionismusstreit' and the German History in Documents abstract all present it as Bernstein's critique of Marxist theory and tactics from 1896, set out in Die Voraussetzungen des Sozialismus (Evolutionary Socialism), which Bernstein himself calls an exposition of the German social democratic revisionists' tendencies. Sources used: that book, Bernstein's articles of the revisionist debate and after (1896 replies to Bax, 1907 on patriotism, 1915 'Revisionism and Nationalism', 1922 on Bolshevism), and the immediate demands of the Erfurt programme, which Bernstein co-drafted and says he does not want to change. Excluded: the Erfurt programme's theoretical part, which he rejected; other revisionists where they differed from him; Bernstein's writings before 1896; the later pejorative uses of 'revisionism' by Leninists, Maoists and Soviet theorists; reformism and post-war social democracy, which are separate subjects.

aliases.name: Revisionismus
aliases.quote: Direkte Konsequenzen hatte der Dresdner Parteitagsbeschluss nicht, da die Resolution den Revisionismus so definierte, dass auch die meisten Anhänger Bernsteins ihr zustimmen konnten.

keyFigures.role: SPD theorist whose 1896-1899 critique of Marxist theory founded revisionism; author of Evolutionary Socialism.
keyFigures.quote: Thus, it came as a shock to his party comrades when Bernstein launched a series of tough criticisms against Marxist theory.

sources.title: The Erfurt Program (1891)
sources.author: Social Democratic Party of Germany; immediate demands co-drafted by Eduard Bernstein
sources.usedFor: Only the immediate (practical) demands, which Bernstein co-drafted and says in Evolutionary Socialism III(d) he does not want to change: suffrage, direct legislation, militia, arbitration, women's legal equality, free expression, religion as a private matter, secular schools, free medical care, graduated taxes, labour protection. sources.author: Eduard Bernstein
sources.usedFor: Bolshevik one-party despotism, suppression of the press, 'new capitalist order'; the 1918 republic as a gain in political freedom.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Bernstein writes that keeping the nation able to defend itself is something social democracy 'never questions, which, indeed, it advocates'.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bernstein's agrarian programme fights entail, privileged estate parishes and hunting privileges, and he defines democracy as a condition where no class holds political privilege.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses would pay for all public expenditure through a graduated income and property tax.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bernstein says he has long held that commodity trade cannot be replaced by an artificially thought-out system of exchange, and keeps the economic self-responsibility of everyone able to work for any period within sight.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Bernstein agrees with Kautsky that no reason will exist for abolishing peasant holdings even after a socialist victory, and wants co-operation to keep small holdings competitive.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter for the individual.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Bernstein says social democracy will, where direct agreement is impossible, 'stand up for settling the difference by means of arbitration', as the Erfurt programme demands.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Bernstein rejects Blanquism and says a politically rightless working class may join small conspiracies but will never develop a socialist movement.

ban-interest.rationale: Bernstein defends the creative side of the credit system against Luxemburg and counts credit associations and the cheapening of interest among the means that keep small peasants competitive.

basic-income.rationale: Bernstein rejects maintaining all the unemployed out of state money and says the economic personal responsibility of all capable of work cannot be given up.

bound-labor.rationale: In his agrarian programme the first task he names is 'the struggle against all the present remnants and supports of feudal landowners', alongside democracy in commune and district.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses include the annual voting of taxes, and he refuses social democracy any share in foreign-policy measures that could be turned to account over the heads of the people's representatives.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Bernstein calls trade unions indispensable organs of the democracy and wants a democratic, socialist party of reform working through representative bodies.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bernstein rejects the expectation of an imminent collapse of bourgeois economy and argues that credit and the extended world market increase capitalism's possibilities of adjustment to crises.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bernstein traces imperialism to capitalist combinations but sees social forces drawing peoples together and says nations no longer lightly go to war, so war is not inevitable.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Bernstein says the socialist movement depends on organisations and conceptions of law that necessarily accompany capitalist evolution, and grounds its prospects on the growth of social wealth and productive forces.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for abolishing all laws that limit or suppress the free expression of opinion.

central-planning.rationale: Bernstein argues the state could not even take over the medium and large enterprises, and agrees that commodity trade has permeated social life too deeply to be replaced by an artificially thought-out system of exchange.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Bernstein argues that for a party keeping up with real evolution 'criticism is indispensable and tradition can become an oppressive burden', to be shelved once inconsistent with what exists.

character-from-environment.rationale: Bernstein says workers 'have the virtues and failings of the economic and social conditions under which they live', which cannot be set aside overnight.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bernstein writes that the higher civilisation can claim a higher right over 'savages', that cultivation rather than conquest gives title to land, and that savage races may be compelled to conform with the rules of higher civilisation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bernstein welcomes compulsory arbitration courts for trade disputes as 'organs for the furtherance of industrial peace' and quotes approvingly that democratic development serves gradually as a substitute for the class war.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bernstein accepts the theory of class wars as part of Marx's pure science but holds that ideological and ethical factors have growing independent weight against economic necessity.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter and make churches private associations, while Bernstein grounds legitimacy in the sovereignty of the people.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Bernstein's workers' patriotism 'cannot be that which seeks the ruling of nationalities by other nationalities', and he rejects redrawing borders on ethnological lines.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Trade unions and cooperatives are central levers of reform in Bernstein's gradual road to socialism.

collective-farming.rationale: He stressed small peasant holdings and voluntary cooperatives helping small farmers, not collectivisation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Bernstein foresees Germany drawing colonial produce from its own colonies, but insists colonisation need not injure the natives and that the settlement and treatment of natives be controlled.

communal-electorates.rationale: Bernstein made equal, universal suffrage the core of democracy, which leaves no place for separate religious electorates.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Bernstein rejects the absolute sovereignty of the municipality and calls a national assembly representing the national interest indispensable, against a federation built from delegates.

conscription.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for educating all to bear arms, and he says training the people to the use of arms is a necessity social democracy advocates.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He calls socialism the heir of liberalism, which made the sovereignty of the people, as Rousseau set it out, 'the fundamental conditions of the legitimacy of every constitution'.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He demanded protection of individuals against arbitrary action of accidental majorities.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Bernstein maintains 'the right of the higher civilisation over the lower' and asks how a socialist can deny it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The Erfurt programme's immediate demands, endorsed by Bernstein, call for abolishing all indirect taxes and customs that sacrifice the community to a privileged few.

death-penalty.rationale: The Erfurt programme's immediate demands, which Bernstein says he does not want to change, include the abolition of capital punishment.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Bernstein favours extending public services and insurance, which divest economic responsibility of its hardness, but in 1891 warned against maintaining all the unemployed out of state money, which would include those who will not work.

decide-locally.rationale: Bernstein expects the municipality to become an ever more important lever of emancipation, but holds that national law must come from the state and that absolute municipal sovereignty is no ideal.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Bernstein argues that the belief abroad that a party is waiting for war to obstruct its own government, by a military strike, may become the greatest menace to peace, and backs national defence.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is 'not only the means but also the substance' of socialism, and the indispensable preliminary condition for it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Bernstein says nearly everyone means more by democracy than a form of government, defining it as the absence of class government and including a notion of justice, equality of rights for all.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He calls the phrase antiquated, says 'the dictatorship of the classes belongs to a lower civilisation' and is 'political atavism', and warns it would mean the dictatorship of club orators and writers.

direct-action.rationale: Bernstein grants that social democracy has a field outside parliament, but says exclusion from representative bodies would make the movement chaotic and jerky instead of a steady advance.

direct-votes.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses include direct legislation by the people through rights of proposal and rejection, beside an elected parliament.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for abolishing all laws that place women at a disadvantage compared with men in public or private law.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bernstein holds that the principle of the economic personal responsibility of all those capable of work cannot be given up at any period within sight, individual responsibility being the return for services rendered by society.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bernstein embraces the liberal principle, set out by Rousseau, that the sovereignty of the people is the fundamental condition of the legitimacy of every constitution.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bernstein insists on 'no rights without duties' and denies the individual is free from all duties to the community, yet holds that duties to the state require rights such as universal suffrage in return.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Bernstein's 1915 essay says the sociological conception leads to free exchange among nations, while the imperialist plans for dividing the world among tariff leagues would tear the peoples apart.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bernstein welcomes the November 1918 revolution in which thrones were smashed and crowns torn away, calling the resulting republic a gain in political freedom for workers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bernstein wants the 'steady strengthening of international law' and an International that takes a positive position on international law and treaties.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Bernstein writes that democracy today includes a notion of justice, 'an equality of rights for all members of the community', which limits majority rule.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bernstein writes that 'the purely ethnological national principle is reactionary in its results' and that dividing mankind nationally by race is anything but a human ideal.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses abolish capital punishment and provide appeal in criminal cases and compensation for the unjustly convicted.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for a graduated income and property tax.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses make medical care, schooling and burial free, though he doubts free legal services are advisable under present conditions.

free-public-college.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses include free education at higher institutions for boys and girls qualified by their abilities.

free-trade.rationale: Bernstein writes that the sociological conception of relations among peoples 'leads necessarily to the policy of free exchange among nations', bringing peoples into closer contact.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Bernstein ties free exchange among nations to the forces drawing peoples into closer community of interest, and tariff leagues to imperialism and the tearing apart of peoples.

gradual-change.rationale: Bernstein holds that important periods in the development of nations cannot be leapt over, that legislation works as a systematic force, and that a steady advance offers more security than a catastrophe.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses give the popular assembly the decision on war and peace.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Bernstein rejects the preference for primitive barbarism over modern civilisation and argues that the worker's condition is capable of improvement and has improved.

independent-unions.rationale: Bernstein saw trade unions as democratic organisations of workers that win gains within capitalism, run by their members.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Bernstein recognises 'only a conditional right of savages to the land occupied by them', since the higher civilisation can claim a higher right and cultivation gives the title to use.

indirect-election.rationale: He held democracy to be both means and substance of socialism and favoured universal direct suffrage over restricted or indirect selection.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Bernstein rejects Bax's calling modern civilisation 'a curse and an evil per se' and the preference for primitive barbarism, acknowledging civilisation's relative acquisitions.

informal-organisation.rationale: He built reform on lasting formal organisations, the party, trade unions and cooperatives, and spoke of the movement as everything.

job-guarantee.rationale: Bernstein calls a right to work in the sense of the state guaranteeing everyone occupation in his calling improbable and 'not even desirable', looking to unions and other organs instead.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Bernstein argues that once all its reductions are made, labour value loses every concrete quality and becomes 'a pure abstract concept', and surplus value a formula resting on a hypothesis.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Bernstein calls the purely ethnological national principle, erecting national states on language and descent, reactionary in its results, preferring a sociological idea of the nation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter and end all public spending for religious purposes.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Bernstein's municipal programme demands that all enterprises of a monopolist character serving the general needs of the members of the municipality be carried out under its own management, and that it constantly widen its services.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Bernstein says the Bolsheviks, while compromising with foreign capitalists, are creating 'a new capitalist order' at a lower level of culture under a despotic party.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He argued economic conditions create only a disposition toward ideas and that ideological and ethical factors have growing independent weight.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bernstein calls democracy 'not only the means but also the substance' of socialism, and Steger stresses his insistence on the tight link between means and ends.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: Bernstein praises the SPD as the most decided Imperial party, keener than any other to transfer legislative authority to the Reich.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Bernstein says social democracy has always opposed militarism in the sense of being ruled by the military or an army set apart from the people.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Bernstein defends Armenian national autonomy against Turkish misrule, and in 1907 calls for the equal democratic right of the nationalities within existing states.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter and secularise the schools.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Bernstein wants municipalities to run monopolist local enterprises and to keep extending their services, and to beat private firms as employers, while private undertakings continue beside them.

municipal-property.rationale: Bernstein backed cooperatives and municipal and state enterprise, not one local-ownership model.

nation-first.rationale: Bernstein says internationalism is no reason to yield to foreign pretensions where important national interests are at stake, yet supports arbitration and every institution working for peace.

national-church-status.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter and treat all religious communities as private associations without public funds.

national-self-determination.rationale: Bernstein grants 'the right of nationality to every people that has shown itself capable of developing or maintaining' a national civilisation, but denies it to races he calls hostile to civilisation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Bernstein wants municipalities to run monopoly enterprises and keep extending their services, and welcomes public education and insurance as divesting economic responsibility of its hardness.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses include the secularisation of schools.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bernstein condemns the Bolsheviks as a despotic party holding power by military dictatorship and allowing no other party, socialist or capitalist, freedom of action.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Bernstein keeps the right of revolution as a natural right that no statute can prohibit, while preferring the path of reform where political rights exist.

organic-representation.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for universal, equal and direct suffrage with proportional representation of parties, and he doubts Proudhon's scheme of delegates from local bodies.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bernstein wants universal suffrage to turn the people's representatives from masters into servants, and endorses the Erfurt demands that the popular assembly decide war and peace and vote taxes yearly.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Steger summarises Bernstein's 'evolutionary' road to socialism through peaceful, parliamentary means and gradual democratic reform; Bernstein calls universal suffrage the alternative to a violent revolution.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Bernstein stressed democratic participation, trade unions and cooperatives as the road to socialism and as workers' self-government.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bernstein condemns the Bolsheviks' 'extermination of the independent Press', and the Erfurt demands he endorses would abolish every law limiting free expression.

party-own-road.rationale: Bernstein says socialist parties have had to adapt to their own countries' conditions, so that 'no programme of action applicable for all countries is possible'.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Bernstein argues that the worker with equal rights 'has a fatherland without ceasing on that account to be a citizen of the world', and that the working class develops a new patriotism of its own.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bernstein upholds the formula 'conversion of the standing armies to citizen armies' as the aim, while pressing for interim measures since disbanding standing armies is now impossible.

person-over-state.rationale: Bernstein says the aim of all socialist measures, even coercive ones, is 'the development and the securing of a free personality'.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Bernstein says feudalism's 'unbending organisations' had to be destroyed, and that what distinguishes socialist organisations from feudal ones is 'their liberalism, their democratic constitution, their accessibility'.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bernstein says the individual is to be free 'from every economic compulsion in his action and choice of a calling', a freedom only possible for all by organisation, so socialism is 'organising liberalism'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bernstein says the complete breaking up of nations is no beautiful dream and that a single world language would lose a source of intellectual enjoyment.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He saw the state as the highest legal authority of the community, so privatised courts are incompatible.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He accepted surplus value as a core of Marx's pure science but criticised the value theory's gaps; revisionists were divided.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bernstein called socialism the heir of liberalism and stressed legality and protection against arbitrary majorities.

property-franchise.rationale: Bernstein defended universal suffrage as the foundation of democratic socialism and opposed class franchises.

property-fundamental.rationale: He wanted property rights protected by common law against arbitrary majorities, but socialism aimed at progressively subordinating private capital to society, so property is not absolute.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property should be protected from arbitrary majorities but capital is subject to democratic social control.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Erfurt demands call for proportional representation, and Bernstein cites social democracy's declaration for it as showing that the dictatorship of the proletariat is an antiquated phrase.

public-ownership.rationale: Bernstein demands that every enterprise of a monopolist character serving the general needs of the community be run by the municipality under its own management, while doubting that the state could take over all large enterprises.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses would abolish every law limiting free expression and declare religion a private matter.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for universal, equal and direct suffrage for all citizens over twenty without distinction of sex.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Bernstein writes that the general legislature of the nation stands above the parish, apportioning its functions, and that law must come from the state as the highest legal authority.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Erfurt programme's immediate demands, which Bernstein says he does not want to change, call for national and international labour protection laws and state supervision of all industrial establishments.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bernstein kept a right of revolution against a government that violated rights, even while preferring legal reform.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bernstein says feudalism had to be destroyed and that social democracy fights the remnants of feudal landowning, while liberal institutions are to be developed further.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter for the individual.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Bernstein writes that for social democracy 'the security of civil freedom has always seemed to it to stand higher than the fulfilment of some economic progress'.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for abolishing all laws that limit or suppress the free expression of opinion.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Bernstein counts the Reichstag's rejection of the Kaiser's bill threatening penal servitude for inciting strikes as confirming his view, and the Erfurt demands he endorses include safeguarding freedom of association.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He wanted socialism judged by experience and logic, valued the movement over a fixed final goal, and criticised dogma.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Bernstein dismisses 'visionary enthusiasm for the state of nature' and the preferability of primitive barbarism, and holds there is no right of hunters over cultivators.

right-to-secede.rationale: Bernstein wants national problems solved 'not by altering the boundaries on the map of Europe' but by altering the constitutions of existing states, and praises Austrian social democracy for countering centrifugal tendencies.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter, end all public spending for church purposes and treat churches as private associations.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Bernstein writes that the liberal organisations of modern society, unlike feudal ones, 'do not need to be destroyed, but only to be further developed'.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: Bernstein argues that where democracy exists the appeal to a revolution by force becomes a meaningless phrase, and quotes approvingly that socialists seek power not by violence and bloodshed but by lawful means.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Bernstein names the exercise of political sovereignty by the workers' class party as a condition of socialism and keeps the conquest of political power by the working classes as a programme demand.

socialized-markets.rationale: He envisioned cooperatives and municipal enterprises coexisting with markets and surviving small firms, not wholesale replacement.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Bernstein rejects anti-militarist propaganda for a military strike as increasing the danger of war, and calls national self-defence a necessity social democracy never questions.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Bernstein writes that the Bolsheviks are creating in Russia 'a new capitalist order which differs from the one only by its being on lower level of culture'.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bernstein defines democracy as the suppression of class government and says universal suffrage turns representatives from masters into servants of the people.

state-harmful.rationale: He held the state is the highest legal authority of the community and the vehicle for social reform, rejecting any anti-statism.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses declare religion a private matter and leave religious communities to run their own affairs.

strong-leader.rationale: Bernstein calls democracy 'the high school of compromise' in which parties learn the limits of their power, and condemns Bolshevik rule as a despotism nearer the old Tsarism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses leave religious communities to regulate their affairs entirely autonomously as private associations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Bernstein's 1922 article condemns Bolshevik rule for suppressing all spiritual life, exterminating the independent press and allowing no other party freedom of action.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Bernstein's 1915 essay sets the policy of free exchange among nations against the imperialist idea of high tariffs, and the Erfurt demands he endorses call for abolishing customs duties.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses include an inheritance tax graduated by the size of the inheritance and the degree of kinship.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Erfurt programme's immediate demands, which Bernstein endorses, call for a graduated income and property tax to meet all public expenditure.

taxation-theft.rationale: Bernstein endorses the Erfurt demands that a graduated income, property and inheritance tax meet all public expenditure.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Bernstein accepted German colonies and the Kiautschou lease as securing German interests, but in 1915 opposed the capitalist nationalism that culminates in imperialism.

total-state.rationale: Bernstein says socialism will create no new bondage, that the aim of all socialist measures is the development and securing of a free personality, and warns against enforced uniformity.

unions-good.rationale: Bernstein calls trade unions 'the democratic element in industry' and 'indispensable organs of the democracy', whose tendency is to destroy the absolutism of capital.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Bernstein writes that a trade union as mistress of a whole branch of production would be a monopolist association, 'antagonistic to socialism and democracy, let its inner constitution be what it may'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Erfurt programme's immediate demands, which Bernstein says he does not want to change, include free medical care, midwifery and medicines.

universal-morality.rationale: Bernstein turns to Kant against dogma and holds that the movement's aims must embody 'a higher view of morals and of legal rights', with responsibility as 'the foundation of the moral law'.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bernstein warns that without strong workers' organisations and mental independence gained in self-government, the dictatorship of the proletariat means 'the dictatorship of club orators and writers'.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses set the voting age at twenty.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: Bernstein says the misery theory has been given up nearly everywhere and that factory legislation shows 'not hopelessness but capability of improvement in the condition of the worker'.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses would abolish every law that places women at a disadvantage compared with men in private law, which includes inheritance and ownership.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Erfurt demands Bernstein endorses call for universal, equal and direct suffrage for all citizens over twenty, 'without distinction of sex'.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Bernstein objects that maintaining all the unemployed out of state money would keep 'everyone that will not find work', and holds to the economic personal responsibility of all those capable of work.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Bernstein says the peasants belong to the working classes and that social democracy must win a great part of them by committing itself to measures that improve the small peasants' position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Bernstein finds that purely productive associations of workers fail economically and morally, and that large industrial undertakings are 'absolutely unfit for the associated management of the employees themselves'; he backs consumer co-operatives instead.

workers-councils.rationale: Bernstein doubts that democracy requires replacing the national assembly with delegates of local and district assemblies, as Marx and Proudhon pictured, and calls a national assembly indispensable.

workers-nation.rationale: Bernstein says socialism 'can and must be national' as the completion of cosmopolitan consciousness, while calling the International of the people a union of nations joined in freedom.

workers-own-party.rationale: Revisionism stayed within the SPD as a working-class party seeking power through democratic reform and trade unions.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Bernstein wants social democracy to appear as what it is, 'a democratic, socialistic party of reform', striving for socialist transformation through democratic and economic reform.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Bernstein says the trade unions aim to destroy the absolutism of capital and to procure for the worker a direct influence in the management of an industry, though not an unconditional right of decision.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism is not heading for a general collapse; credit, cartels and the world market make crises less likely.
missingStatements.rationale: Bernstein rejected collapse theory on exactly these grounds, a defining revisionist break with orthodox Marxism.

missingStatements.text: The ultimate goal of a political movement matters less than the movement and its day-to-day reforms.
missingStatements.rationale: His famous line that the ultimate aim is nothing and the movement everything.

missingStatements.text: Socialism is fundamentally an ethical ideal rather than a historical inevitability.
missingStatements.rationale: Bernstein turned to Kantian ethics and rejected strict historical determinism.
missingStatements.declined: Philosophical claim already weighed by material-conditions-drive-history, where the audit answers split (0) for Bernstein's mixed view; not added to keep the bank lean.

notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-09) bringing a pre-rules audit up to rules 5. The first pass rested partly on two Wikipedia articles (s5, s6), which are kept only for the review history; answers that rested on them, or on a general value such as 'democracy is the substance of socialism' that does not settle the statement, were re-sourced from Bernstein's own texts or nulled (reviewHistory keeps the earlier versions). Themes searched: economy (ownership, co-operatives, municipal enterprise, taxation, welfare and the right to work, value theory, crises, trade), government (suffrage, representation, direct legislation, federalism and municipal autonomy, dictatorship, revolution), world (nation, patriotism, colonies, war, arbitration, international law), society and liberty (religion, free expression, women's legal equality), and culture, ecology and technology, on which the revisionist texts are silent. The Erfurt programme's immediate demands are used because Bernstein co-drafted them and states in Evolutionary Socialism that he does not wish to change them, noting only doubts about free legal services; they are answered at medium confidence. Bernstein's colonial views (a 'higher right' of higher civilisation, a reformed socialist colonial policy) are recorded as stated, as Haag's FES article describes the revisionist current. Not used: Bernstein's 1890 and 1895 articles (before the revisionist debate), his 1897 essays on Marx (about Marx's views), and the hostile accounts of Lenin, Luxemburg and later anti-revisionists. The Dictionary of the History of Ideas entry 'Marxist Revisionism' (Kindersley) could not be reached (the University of Virginia host returned no content). The original 'Problems of Socialism' articles and Bernstein's later Reichstag speeches were not found as open full text. Critics, notably Maoists, used 'revisionism' pejoratively for any deviation from orthodoxy; those uses are other subjects.
